## What are the five CMS TEAM procedure categories?

<BlogChartFigure src={"/charts/team-episode-volume.png"} alt={"Bar chart of CMS TEAM episode volume by procedure category"} caption={"Episode counts concentrate in LEJR; financial planning still requires dedicated workstreams for fracture, spine, CABG, and bowel."} source={"Rainfall Health; CMS-derived 2023 baseline episode volumes at TEAM hospitals."} />

TEAM does **not** bundle all of Medicare. It holds mandated hospitals accountable for five surgical episode categories across a **30-day post-discharge** window: **lower extremity joint replacement (LEJR)**, **surgical hip/femur fracture treatment (SHFFT)**, **spinal fusion**, **coronary artery bypass graft (CABG)**, and **major bowel procedures**.

If your service line is not on that list, TEAM may still touch you indirectly (shared PAC capacity, enterprise analytics), but the reconciliation math attaches to these five. For the legal definition of an episode, see *What is an episode of care?*

<BlogFastFacts label={"Fast Facts — Five episodes"} items={["LEJR — highest national volume (~204k TEAM-hospital episodes baseline across all five","LEJR majority share)","SHFFT — geriatric, frail, high PAC and delirium risk","Spinal fusion — device + rehab variability; outlier risk","CABG — lower count, high spend, cardiac rehab critical","Major bowel — infection and readmission sensitive","Window — discharge + 30 days (not 90-day BPCI-style for all historical models)"]} />

## LEJR: why hips and knees dominate the conversation

**Lower extremity joint replacement** is the volume engine. Most TEAM hospitals will live or die financially on how consistently they discharge LEJR patients to home with robust therapy — not on shaving six minutes of OR time. Prior mandatory CJR evidence showed reductions in institutional PAC use under bundles (Finkelstein et al., 2018).

Surgeon champions need weekly visibility into discharge destination, home-health starts within 24–48 hours, and 30-day returns. CFOs need target-price literacy: CMS blends hospital history with regional benchmarks and applies a discount factor — see the episode-cost analysis for dollar ranges.

## Hip fracture (SHFFT): the geriatric stress test

**Surgical hip/femur fracture treatment** episodes concentrate medical complexity: frailty, delirium risk, skilled-nursing defaults, and goals-of-care ambiguity. Hospitals that treat fracture like “urgent ortho” without geriatric protocols will fund SNF days they cannot recover.

Operational must-haves: ortho-geri co-management, early PT, delirium prevention, and honest goals-of-care before acceptance of transfer patients who cannot rehabilitate.

## Spinal fusion: device spend meets rehab variability

Spine episodes combine implantable-device cost variation with heterogeneous rehab trajectories. Indication discipline and implant formularies matter as much as discharge planning. Many systems under-invest in spine episode analytics because LEJR hogs the dashboard — a mistake when a handful of fusion outliers erase LEJR gains.

## CABG and major bowel: lower volume, real money

**CABG** volumes are smaller than LEJR but average episode spend is high. Cardiac rehab enrollment, early follow-up, and infection surveillance are the TEAM levers — not just STS operative metrics.

**Major bowel** episodes are sensitive to SSI, anastomotic complications, and readmissions. ERAS pathways and wound surveillance after discharge are finance projects as much as surgery projects.

<div class="blog-table-scroll not-prose">

| Category | Clinical focus | Primary TEAM risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LEJR | Elective hip/knee replacement | Institutional PAC overuse; volume scale |
| SHFFT | Hip/femur fracture surgery | Frailty, SNF defaults, delirium |
| Spinal fusion | Fusion procedures | Implant + rehab outliers |
| CABG | Coronary bypass | High spend; rehab gaps |
| Major bowel | Major intestinal surgery | Infection / readmission |

</div>

## How should hospitals organize ownership?

Give each category a **named dyad** (surgeon leader + administrative owner) with a shared episode P&L. Do not bury TEAM inside a generic “value committee” that meets monthly. Tie preparation checklists to Track selection (see track comparison) and use the episode-volume and episode-cost analyses for board-level quantification.

## Frequently asked questions

### What five procedures does CMS TEAM cover?

LEJR (hip/knee replacement), SHFFT (surgical hip/femur fracture), spinal fusion, CABG, and major bowel procedures.

### Which procedure has the most volume?

LEJR is the national volume engine at TEAM hospitals; hospitals should still run dedicated workstreams for the other four.

### How long is a TEAM episode?

The model’s accountability window runs through 30 days after discharge for included episodes — confirm coding details against CMS specifications for your cases.

### Where can I see cost ranges?

See Rainfall’s “What a CMS TEAM Episode Actually Costs” analysis for procedure-level spend ranges.
